items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: there was another fellow there we'd call Duke something -- this fellow could take "Onward Christian Soldiers", and really swing it.

ctx.x: an ordinary piano, that's all most poor people in those days could afford.

So, we'd play at these parties. Well, each time we'd meet other fellows playing at the parties, and we learned how to, what you call, swing. There was a guy -- or, stride. There was a guy there that -- for -- a fellow named Rawson, Ralph Rawson. He came over from New York, and he -- and there was another fellow there we'd call Duke something -- this fellow could take "Onward Christian Soldiers", and really swing it. What we called swing today, but stride, but stride, and I'll tell you about this stride business…

That was the alto horn. And the bass would go -- (sings) But, so, and then the right hand was playing the melody. And these things happened so that we got so that we could master those things pretty good. And the next thing, we had time. Because a lot of times, there was no drums with you. And if there was drums, they couldn't afford drums, because the houses and the walls was too thin, and first thing you'd know, somebody else would be complaining about the drums. And so, if you had drums, you wouldn't last much…
